description: Open-source cookie consent for Next.js, React and plain JavaScript: a consent banner, Google Consent Mode v2, and third-party scripts loaded only after consent.
rules: Import from @cookieyes/nextjs in Next.js apps, @cookieyes/react in other React apps, and @cookieyes/core for plain JavaScript, Vue, Svelte or Angular.
Next.js apps import "@cookieyes/nextjs/styles.css", never "@cookieyes/react/styles.css". Without a stylesheet import the banner renders unstyled and nothing warns.
In Next.js, call initCookieYes() in a file that starts with "use client" and render it from the root layout, which stays a Server Component.
Use mode: "cookie-only" (no backend) or mode: "self-hosted" with an apiUrl. mode: "offline" is deprecated; write "cookie-only".

Load third-party tools with presets from @cookieyes/scripts (ga4, googleTagManager, googleAds, metaPixel, clarity, posthog, segment, customScript) in the integrations option. builtInIntegrations is deprecated.
Remove vendor snippets pasted into the HTML by hand; the integration adds the script itself.
For GA4, GTM or Google Ads add the Consent Mode default: <GoogleConsentMode /> from @cookieyes/nextjs/server in Next.js, bootstrapGoogleConsentMode() from @cookieyes/scripts elsewhere.
Google presets default to consentMode: "advanced", which loads the tag at once and relies on Consent Mode. Pass consentMode: "basic" when nothing may reach Google before the visitor accepts.
If GA4 or Google Ads is loaded inside a GTM container, use googleTagManager() only, not also ga4() or googleAds().
A custom integration uses load: "afterConsent" and a category that exists in the categories list, or it never loads.
Unit-test consent logic with @cookieyes/test: createConsentTest(), or createReactConsentTest() from @cookieyes/test/react, and reset state after each test.
